## Summary

Patch release (v2.9.2) fixing a Windows issue where the STT status pill showed **"STT needs attention"** whenever AssemblyAI was the speech-to-text provider, even though transcription worked fine.

## Fixes

- **AssemblyAI "STT needs attention" pill on Windows** — the system-audio (interviewer) capture emits audio chunks as short as 20ms, which AssemblyAI rejects with an *Input Duration Violation* (it requires 50–1000ms frames). Each rejection was counted toward a 5-error threshold that flipped the channel to "failed" and surfaced the pill. Audio is now buffered and forwarded to AssemblyAI in valid 50–1000ms frames, so the pill no longer appears and system-audio transcription stays stable.

## Technical

- `electron/audio/AssemblyAIStreamingSTT.ts` — frames inbound audio into AssemblyAI-compatible 50–1000ms chunks
- `electron/audio/__tests__/AssemblyAIFrameAccumulation.test.mjs` — new tests covering the floor/ceiling bounds, real 640-byte system-audio chunk coalescing, and accumulator cleanup

## ⚠️ Windows Installation (Unsigned Build)

When running the installer on Windows, you might see a "Windows protected your PC" warning from Microsoft Defender SmartScreen saying it prevented an unrecognized app from starting.

Since this is an unsigned build, this is expected. You can safely ignore it by clicking **More info** and then **Run anyway**.
